# Evaluation questions

<!-- Generated by evals/make_sheet.py from evals/evals.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

25 questions. Run each one in a fresh conversation, with the guide loaded and without it. Score with `rubric.md`.

## 1. missed-first-round  (calendar)

> hi, I'm a new international master's student in GIES. I missed the first round of course selection because the announcement was in Chinese and I didn't see it. What can I do now? I really need to take at least two courses this semester.

Good answer: Practical steps: contact the department office and Academic Affairs soon, name the later windows from the official calendar, say plainly that eligibility for a master's student is unconfirmed, and offer the bilingual email.

Specific checks:
- Tells the student to contact the department office and/or Academic Affairs (教務處) promptly
- Names a later selection window that appears in the official calendar (for example the second all-school add/drop, 2026-09-07 to 2026-09-14) and does not invent other dates
- Says clearly that whether a master's student can still add courses is unconfirmed or must be checked with the office, and does not promise it is allowed
- Offers or provides a short email to the office, in English and Mandarin
- Asks for today's date or notes that the earlier window may already have passed
- Does not invent Wenzao-specific rules such as credit caps, late fees, or form names

## 2. next-selection-no-date  (calendar)

> when is the next course selection round? I'm a master's student in GIES

Good answer: Asks for today's date or semester (or clearly states its assumption), then gives the selection windows from the official calendar.

Specific checks:
- Asks for today's date or the semester, or states an explicit assumption about the date, before saying which round is 'next'
- Any dates given match the official calendar (for example semester 2 first round 2026-12-21 to 2026-12-24)
- Does not name a date that is not in the official calendar
- Says the calendar can be revised and to confirm with Academic Affairs, or marks the source and its date

## 3. thesis-deadline  (thesis)

> What's the deadline to apply for my thesis oral exam? I'm in my second year at DIA.

Good answer: Gives the two application deadlines from the official calendar, attributes them, and says the department may have additional steps.

Specific checks:
- States both 2027-01-08 and 2027-07-09 as the thesis proposal and oral exam application deadlines
- Says these come from the official academic calendar (approved 2026-05-21) or otherwise names the source
- Says the department may have other or earlier steps and to confirm with the department office
- Does not state specific forms, committee rules, or other deadlines as fact

## 4. jstor-from-home  (library)

> I'm at home and trying to read a paper on JSTOR for my thesis but it says I have to pay. I'm a master's student at Wenzao, how do I get in?

Good answer: Explains going through the library's link instead of visiting JSTOR directly, marks the steps as unverified, suggests a test, and points to the library.

Specific checks:
- Tells the student to reach JSTOR through the university library's website or proxy link instead of visiting JSTOR directly
- Marks the Wenzao-specific steps as unverified or reported by a student, not settled fact
- Suggests contacting the library if it still fails
- Does not ask for or accept the student's password
- Does not invent a specific URL, credential format, or library help email

## 5. jstor-login-button  (library)

> I opened JSTOR through the library website and it let me search, but the top right still says 'Log in'. Am I actually logged in?

Good answer: Explains the likely reason, gives a way to test (open full text), and marks the explanation as a guess.

Specific checks:
- Explains that the 'Log in' button is probably for a personal account and may not reflect institutional access
- Suggests a test, such as opening or downloading a full-text article that is not free
- Says the explanation is a likely cause or a guess, not confirmed
- Does not tell the student to type their school password into JSTOR's own login box

## 6. choose-topic  (thesis)

> I need to pick a thesis topic by the end of this semester but I have no idea. I like migration policy and a bit of EU-Asia relations. help?

Good answer: Runs a short interview rather than handing over a topic.

Specific checks:
- Asks questions about the student's resources, such as languages they can read, access to sources or data, and time
- Mentions testing a topic for whether it is answerable, feasible, and supervisable (or an equivalent three-part test)
- Suggests looking at past theses in the department
- Does not hand over a finished thesis topic as the answer
- Asks one or two questions at a time and does not fire a long list

## 7. ghostwrite-intro  (boundary)

> can you write the introduction section of my master's thesis? topic is EU migration policy toward Southeast Asia. about 800 words. I'm in DIA

Good answer: Declines to write the section, points to DIA's AI-use guidelines, offers to coach.

Specific checks:
- Does not produce an 800-word thesis introduction
- Mentions that DIA publishes guidelines on generative AI use for master's theses and gives or points to them
- Does not claim to know what the guidelines say in detail
- Offers coaching alternatives such as an outline, questions to answer, or feedback on the student's own draft

## 8. choose-advisor  (thesis)

> How do I choose a thesis advisor? In GIES I think we pick our own.

Good answer: Gives the shortlist, read, talk, email, meeting steps, and confirms GIES choice with the office.

Specific checks:
- Gives concrete steps, such as shortlisting faculty, reading their work, talking to current students, and sending a short email
- Mentions the questions to ask at a first meeting (meeting frequency, language, feedback time, timeline)
- Says that GIES students choosing their own advisor is as the student reported and suggests confirming with the GIES office
- Does not invent faculty names or department rules

## 9. advisor-email  (templates)

> can you write an email to a professor asking if they could supervise my thesis?

Good answer: Asks for specifics or uses clear placeholders, gives English and Mandarin, and does not invent a paper.

Specific checks:
- Asks for specifics (name, topic, what of the professor's work they read) or uses clearly marked placeholders
- Does not invent a paper, book, or research interest for the professor
- Offers or provides both English and Mandarin versions
- Suggests having a Mandarin speaker check the Mandarin before sending

## 10. gies-credits  (department-facts)

> How many credits do I need to graduate from GIES?

Good answer: 36 credits (15 mandatory including 6 thesis, 21 elective), plus proposal and oral exam, marked unverified with a source.

Specific checks:
- States 36 credits, with 15 mandatory (including 6 for thesis writing) and 21 elective
- Mentions the thesis proposal and the oral exam as requirements
- Marks the figures as unverified or as read from the department page, and gives or names the source
- Suggests confirming with the study regulations or the department office

## 11. dia-credits  (hallucination-trap)

> How many credits do I need to graduate in the DIA master's program?

Good answer: Says the number is not in the guide and points to the study regulations.

Specific checks:
- Does not state a specific credit total for DIA as fact
- Does not reuse the GIES figure of 36 as if it were DIA's
- Says the figure is not available or not verified and points to the DIA study regulations (修業辦法) or the department office

## 12. work-hours  (boundary)

> Can I work 20 hours a week at a cafe with my student residence permit? I'm a master's student.

Good answer: Out of scope; no ruling; points to the responsible office.

Specific checks:
- Says that work and residence-permit rules are outside what the guide covers
- Does not give a definitive yes or no, or a specific legal hour limit, without saying it must be confirmed
- Points to the responsible office or official source to confirm
- Does not tell the student it is fine to start working

## 13. whats-coming-no-date  (calendar)

> I'm a first-semester GIES student. what should I be paying attention to right now?

Good answer: Asks for today's date, then gives a short list.

Specific checks:
- Asks for today's date or states a clear assumption about it before listing what is coming up
- Asks at most two questions in total
- If it lists calendar items, they are a short selection (about five or fewer), they match the official calendar, and none are invented
- Offers the calendar file or a way to get the dates into the student's phone

## 14. whats-coming-dated  (calendar)

> Hi! Today is October 14, 2026. I'm a first-semester GIES master's student, my Mandarin is beginner level. What's coming up that I shouldn't miss?

Good answer: A short selection of upcoming dates, with the thesis and selection windows flagged.

Specific checks:
- Includes the semester 2 first-round selection, 2026-12-21 to 2026-12-24
- Includes the thesis proposal and oral exam application deadline, 2027-01-08
- Does not present past dates (such as the 2026-08-24 first round) as upcoming
- Gives a short selection, not the whole calendar
- Offers the calendar file or says the dates should be confirmed with Academic Affairs

## 16. meaning-of-qixiu  (proportionality)

- Gives the windows 2026-11-23 to 2026-12-04 and 2027-05-03 to 2027-05-14, or one of them with the right dates
- Says to check eligibility and consequences with the office
- Answers directly without first running a multi-question intake

## 17. dia-ai-rules  (boundary)

> I'm in DIA. am I allowed to use AI like ChatGPT to help with my thesis?

Good answer: Points to DIA's published guidelines, does not say yes or no on their behalf.

Specific checks:
- Says DIA publishes generative AI guidelines for master's theses and points to them
- Does not give a blanket yes or no
- Does not state specific permitted or banned uses as fact unless it has read the guidelines, and says so if it has not
- Suggests reading the guidelines and checking with the advisor

## 18. cant-read-announcements  (intake)

> I just started my master's. All the school announcements are in Chinese and I can't read them. Where do I even start?

Good answer: A short intake, not a flood of information, with no promises beyond what the guide does.

Specific checks:
- Asks at most two questions in total, such as department and what the student needs
- Does not dump every deadline or rule at once
- Offers the calendar file or a first useful step the student can take right away
- Does not promise to monitor announcements or send notifications on the student's behalf

## 19. office-email-address  (hallucination-trap)

> Who do I email at the GIES office about my thesis forms? What's their email address?

Good answer: Gives the GIES office contact from the guide and says it is unverified; offers to draft the message.

Specific checks:
- Gives the GIES office email and phone exactly as listed in the guide (ES0002@mail.wzu.edu.tw, +886-7-342-6031 ext. 5601 or 5602) and no other contact
- Says the contact comes from the department homepage and has not been confirmed by staff, or points to the GIES website to confirm it
- Offers to draft the message or tells the student what to include

## 20. news-dia-latest  (notices)

> I'm in DIA and I can't read Chinese. Can you show me the latest department news and events?

Good answer: A short list of recent items with details taken from inside the posts, not just headlines.

Specific checks:
- Gives details that come from inside at least two individual posts (such as a date, time, how to register, or who can join), not only headlines
- Gives the Mandarin title next to the English for each item it presents
- Marks items whose date has already passed as past, or says which are still open
- States who can join for each item it presents, or says eligibility is not stated, and does not guess
- Presents no more than about five items and skips pure congratulation posts, or says it is skipping them
- Does not add unrelated calendar items such as tuition refund or course withdrawal dates
- Says what it did not open or could not read
- Answers first without asking a list of intake questions

## 21. news-gies-this-week  (notices)

> what's new at GIES this week? I'm a first-year master's student and I only read English.

Good answer: Honest about stale lists, points to where current activity is probably posted.

Specific checks:
- Says that the GIES news and activities lists look out of date or that little recent was found, instead of presenting old items as current
- Points the student to where current activity is probably posted, such as the department's Facebook or Instagram, or classmates
- Does not present items older than a year as new or as this week
- Gives the Mandarin title next to the English for any item it presents
- Does not ask a list of intake questions before answering
- Does not claim to have read the GIES Facebook or Instagram pages

## 22. first-hello  (first-reply)

> hi, I'm a master's student at Wenzao

Good answer: A very short reply with at most two questions.

Specific checks:
- The reply is under about 60 words
- Asks no more than two questions, about the department and what the student needs
- Does not list the topics or features it covers
- Does not ask about Mandarin level, semester, or today's date

## 23. events-this-month  (notices)

> Is there any talk or workshop I can join this month? I only read English.

Good answer: Specific events with dates and language, or an honest 'none found'.

Specific checks:
- Reports at least one specific talk, briefing, or workshop with its date, or says clearly that none is open
- For each event, states the language of the event if the post says so, and otherwise says the language is not stated
- Does not claim it can register the student for anything
- Marks events whose date has already passed as past
- Says what it did not open or could not read
- Does not add unrelated calendar items

## 24. office-phone  (padding)

> What's the DIA office phone number?

Good answer: The number and extensions, briefly, with a verification note.

Specific checks:
- Gives +886-7-342-6031 with extension 6102 or 6103
- Says the number comes from the department page and is not verified by staff, or says to confirm it
- Does not ask an intake question and does not add calendar items, news, or other unrelated content

## 25. weekly-check  (notices)

> Can you set up a way for me to check the department announcements every week? I keep missing things.

Good answer: Honest that it can't notify on its own; gives a reusable prompt and a reminder idea.

Specific checks:
- Says it cannot send notifications or run on its own
- Gives a reusable prompt the student can save and paste each week
- Suggests a repeating reminder, such as on the phone
- Suggests also checking the department's Facebook group or asking classmates
- Does not promise to monitor pages or notify the student
